name: DeleteDialog
title: Blocks/Edit/DeleteDialog
summary: The destructive confirmation a resource list uses for Delete: a warning `Alert`, a sentence naming what goes with the resource and a Help Center link, then a prompt that shows the resource name in code type with a `CopyButton` beside it and an input the user must match before Delete enables. Every resource list, a folder of files and a table of records open it from the row Delete action; the title reads Delete plus the resource kind, and a container that holds other items passes its own consequence sentence. Delete shows its loading state while the request runs (Cancel and the input are locked, the dialog cannot be dismissed), then closes with a success toast; a refused delete keeps the dialog and the typed name and swaps the warning for a danger `Alert` saying why (Error). The typed confirmation resets each time the dialog opens, so the content stays put while it closes. Built from `ConfirmDialog` (the body in its default slot, its own Cancel and Delete buttons with `loading` and `disabled`), `Alert`, `CopyButton`, `Input` and `Button`; closed by default behind a visible danger trigger. The SettingsRow variant is the settings-page delete: an outlined `Item` row opens the same `ConfirmDialog` with a labelled `Field` + `Input` in its body.

variants.name: SettingsRow
variants.summary: The danger-zone delete of a settings page: an outlined `Item` row under the page's `PageHeader` names what the delete removes and holds the danger trigger, and the medium `ConfirmDialog` it opens stacks a warning `Alert` (with the Help Center link) over a labelled `Field` + `Input` asking for the exact resource name, with Delete disabled until the typed name matches and loading while it runs. The field clears every time the dialog opens. Built from `PageHeader`, `Item`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Alert`, `Field`, `Input` and `Button`. The page is a page body for ConsoleLayout.

variants.name: Error
variants.summary: A delete the server refuses (the resource is still in use): the dialog stays open with the typed name kept, the warning gives way to a danger `Alert` saying what blocks the delete and how to fix it, and Delete can run again.
